sub: Named after “the day of Jumuʿah”, Friday, in ayah 9
theme: Allah’s favour in sending a Messenger ﷺ to teach and purify an unlettered people, a warning against holding scripture without living by it, and the command to leave trade for the Friday prayer.
story: Revealed in Madinah, reportedly in two parts. Ayat 1–8 came around the conquest of Khaybar; Abū Hurayrah, recently Muslim, was sitting with the Prophet ﷺ when they were revealed.

Ayat 9–11 reportedly came years earlier, soon after the move to Madinah. One Friday, while the Prophet ﷺ was giving the sermon, a trade caravan arrived with drums, and most people rushed out. Only about twelve men stayed.
The surah reminds believers of the gift of the Messenger ﷺ, warns them not to treat their book as some before them did, and teaches them to put Allah’s remembrance before trade.

sections.title: Allah sent the unlettered a Messenger who recites, purifies and teaches them
sections.meaning: Everything glorifies Allah, the King, the Holy, the Mighty, the Wise. He sent to the unlettered Arabs a Messenger from among them, reciting His ayat, purifying them, and teaching them the Book and wisdom, though they had been clearly lost. The message also reaches others yet to join them. This is Allah’s favour.
points: Everything glorifies Allah: the King, the Holy, the Mighty, the Wise
A Messenger from the unlettered: recites, purifies, teaches the Book and wisdom
And to others who have not yet joined them
That is Allah’s favour, given to whom He wills
sections.matters: It names the three jobs of the Prophet ﷺ: reciting, purifying and teaching. It shows that guidance is Allah’s gift, owned by no nation, and that it reaches every later generation that joins the first believers.
sections.story: When ayah 3 was recited, the Companions asked who “the others” were. After they asked three times, the Prophet ﷺ put his hand on Salmān al-Fārisī: if faith were at the Pleiades, men from these people would reach it.
explained: The surah opens with yusabbiḥu, in the present tense: creation keeps glorifying Allah, al-Malik, the King who owns and runs everything, and al-Quddūs, free of every flaw. He sent among the ummiyyīn, the unlettered Arabs with no scripture, a Messenger from themselves whose lineage and honesty they knew.

He recites Allah’s ayat to them, purifies them from shirk and bad character, and teaches them the Book and the ḥikmah, the wisdom of his Sunnah. A lost people became leaders in knowledge. The same blessing reaches later believers, Arab and non-Arab, who join them. That is Allah’s favour to whom He wills.
teaches: The Prophet ﷺ came to recite, purify and teach.
Learning the Quran should change your character, not only your knowledge.
Guidance is Allah’s favour; no people owns it.
Later believers can join the first generation in Allah’s blessing.
sections.hook: Ayah 1 has four names in a row: al-Malik, al-Quddūs, al-ʿAzīz, al-Ḥakīm. Ayah 3 ends with the last two. As-Ṣaff began sabbaḥa (past); this surah begins yusabbiḥu (present).

sections.title: Ignoring the Torah: a donkey carrying books; they won’t wish for death
sections.meaning: Those given the Torah who didn’t live by it are like a donkey loaded with books it cannot use. They claim to be Allah’s favourites; if so, let them wish for death. They never will, because of their deeds. The death they run from will meet them, and then comes the account.
points: Given the Torah but didn’t carry it: a donkey loaded with books
A wretched example; Allah doesn’t guide wrongdoers
If you are Allah’s chosen friends, then wish for death
They never will, because of what their hands sent ahead
The death you flee will meet you; then you return to Allah
sections.matters: After praising a people taught by the Messenger ﷺ, it shows what happens when a community holds a scripture but does not act on it. The lesson reaches anyone who carries knowledge without practising it, and reminds everyone that death cannot be escaped.
sections.story: Reportedly revealed around the conquest of Khaybar, addressing the Jews of Arabia after their last stronghold fell. They claimed to be Allah’s special friends and that Paradise was theirs alone.
explained: Ḥummilū at-Tawrāh: they were entrusted with the Torah, to learn it and act on it, then did not carry it. They are like a donkey carrying asfār, large books. It bears the weight but gains nothing. They are worse, since the donkey cannot understand and they could.

They claimed to be awliyāʾ of Allah above all people. So the challenge: if that is true, wish for death, since a true friend of Allah longs to meet Him. They will never wish it, knowing their deeds. Yet the death they run from will meet them, and the Knower of the unseen will tell them what they did.
teaches: Carrying knowledge without acting on it is a burden, not an honour.
Claims of being Allah’s favourites mean nothing without deeds.
This challenge was specific; believers are told not to wish for death.
Death cannot be escaped, so prepare for the return to Allah.
sections.hook: Ayah 5 says “carry” three times: ḥummilū, lam yaḥmilūhā, yaḥmilu asfārā. Ayat 6 and 8 both open with “Qul” (Say). Page 553 ends at ayah 8.

sections.title: At Friday’s call leave trade for prayer; some ran to a caravan
sections.meaning: At the Friday call, go to Allah’s remembrance and leave trade. After the prayer, spread out, seek His bounty and remember Him often. Once, some rushed to a caravan mid-sermon, leaving the Prophet ﷺ standing. What Allah has is better, and He is the best provider.
points: At the Friday call, go to Allah’s remembrance and leave trade
After the prayer, spread out and seek Allah’s bounty
Remember Allah often, so you may succeed
They rushed to trade or amusement and left you standing
What Allah has is better; He is the best provider
sections.matters: This is the Quran’s command for Jumuʿah. It sets the balance: work is allowed and even encouraged, but when Allah calls, business stops. It closes by correcting a real lapse, reminding that provision comes from Allah, not the marketplace.
sections.story: One Friday, as the Prophet ﷺ gave the sermon, a caravan arrived during a food shortage, announced with drums. People hurried out to it, leaving only about twelve men. Reportedly the sermon then came after the prayer, and afterwards it was moved before it.
explained: Jumuʿah, the day of gathering, was given to this ummah. When the adhān is called, fa-sʿaw: head to Allah’s remembrance, the sermon and prayer, with full attention, not by running. Dharū al-bayʿ: leave off trade and anything that distracts. That is better for you.

Once the prayer is done, spread out and seek Allah’s bounty, remembering Him often even while trading. Some once did the opposite: a caravan came during the sermon and they rushed to it, leaving the Prophet ﷺ standing on the minbar. Tell them: what is with Allah is better, and He is the best of providers.
teaches: When the Friday call comes, drop everything and go.
Go to prayer with calm and dignity, not rushing.
Earning a living after prayer is part of seeking Allah’s bounty.
Keep remembering Allah while you work and trade.
Provision comes from Allah, not from skipping worship.
sections.hook: Ayah 9 starts page 554 with “O you who have believed.” Trade runs through the section: al-bayʿ (9), then tijārah and lahw, each twice, in ayah 11.

groups.text: Everything in the heavens and earth glorifies Allah, the King, the Holy, the Mighty, the Wise.
He sent a Messenger to the unlettered to recite, purify, and teach the Book and wisdom.
His message reaches others yet to join them. That is Allah’s great favour.
Those who held the Torah but didn’t act on it are like a donkey carrying books.
Claim to be Allah’s friends? Then wish for death. They won’t, but death will still meet them.
At the Friday call, leave trade for Allah’s remembrance; after prayer, seek His bounty and remember Him often.
Some left the Prophet ﷺ standing for a caravan. What Allah has is better; He is the best provider.

1.explain: Yusabbiḥu: keeps glorifying, in the present tense for continuity. Everything declares Allah’s purity. Al-Malik: the King who owns and controls all. Al-Quddūs: the Holy, free of every flaw. Al-ʿAzīz, al-Ḥakīm: the Mighty, the Wise.

2.explain: Al-ummiyyīn: the Arabs, a people who mostly could not read or write and had no scripture. From them came a Messenger reciting His ayat, purifying them from shirk and bad character, and teaching the Book and wisdom (the Sunnah).

3.explain: Wa ākharīna minhum: others who have not yet joined them, in time or in rank: later believers, non-Arabs among them. Asked who they were, the Prophet ﷺ placed his hand on Salmān al-Fārisī.

4.explain: Faḍl Allāh: Allah’s favour. Sending the Prophet ﷺ and guiding people through him is a gift Allah gives to whom He wills, greater than health or wealth. No people can claim it as their own.

5.explain: Asfār: large books. Those entrusted with the Torah read it but didn’t act on it, including its news of the Prophet ﷺ. Like a donkey under books, they bear the load without benefit. Allah does not guide the wrongdoers.

6.explain: Hādū: those who are Jews. If they truly are Allah’s favourites above all people, let them wish for death, the gateway to the Hereafter. Or it means: pray for death on whichever side is wrong.

7.explain: They will never wish for it, because of what their hands sent ahead: their disbelief and sins. They know what awaits them. Allah knows the wrongdoers well; nothing of their wrong is hidden from Him.

8.explain: Tafirrūna minhu: you run from it. Running from death only brings you face to face with it. Then you return to the Knower of the unseen and the seen, who will tell you everything you did.

9.explain: Nūdiya: the call, the adhān given as the imam sits on the minbar. Fa-sʿaw: go with care and attention, not running. Dhikr Allāh here is the sermon and prayer. Dharū al-bayʿ: buying and selling stop once the call is made.

10.explain: Once the prayer is finished, fa-ntashirū: spread out in the land and seek Allah’s bounty. This is permission, not an order. Keep remembering Allah much, even in the marketplace, so that you may succeed.

11.explain: Lahw: amusement, here the drums announcing the caravan. Infaḍḍū: they scattered to it, leaving the Prophet ﷺ standing in the sermon, which shows the sermon is given standing. What Allah has is better than any deal.
11.why: One Friday during a food shortage, a caravan from Syria, reportedly Diḥyah al-Kalbī’s before he became Muslim, arrived with drums while the Prophet ﷺ was preaching. Almost everyone left; about twelve men stayed. Reports differ on the number.
